findings.description: The 'data' bucket declares no ACL, no public access block, and no bucket policy restriction; the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. Combined with the customer master data object uploaded to it, this exposes sensitive data to anonymous readers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so account-level protections against public ACLs and policies are not enforced for it.
Versioning is disabled, so objects containing sensitive customer data can be overwritten or deleted (including maliciously) with no recovery or tamper evidence.

A file named customer-master.xlsx, containing apparent customer master records, is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket, exposing sensitive data at rest and to anonymous access.
The object is uploaded without specifying kms_key_id or server-side encryption, and the target bucket has no default encryption rule, so it is stored unencrypted.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource guards this bucket, leaving it vulnerable to accidental public ACL or policy grants despite the private ACL.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to financial data cannot be detected or investigated.
The operations bucket defines no default server-side encryption, so its objects are stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so public ACLs or bucket policies could later be applied without being blocked.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, leaving no audit trail of object-level access.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data sets stored there are not encrypted at rest by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so nothing prevents public ACLs or policies from being applied.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central log bucket itself has no access logging configured, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would go unrecorded.
The log bucket uses the log-delivery-write canned ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving audit data without account-level protection against public grants.
None of the buckets enforce aws:SecureTransport via a bucket policy, so objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
